To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fatigue process is the result of the competition between crack growth (microdamage development and growth) and crack healing (microdamage healing).
the fatigue process is viewed, in the case of asphalt concrete mixtures, as the result of competing processes of microcrack damage and microdamage healing.
The rate of healing is directly proportional to the surface energy of the bitumen and the rate of damage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of micromechanics to the fatigue problem.
the mechanism of healing in asphalt mixtures and its influence on fatigue damage.
the development of a fundamental understanding of the mechanism of healing in bituminous mixtures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanism of healing is a function of the mixture surface energy.
the fatigue damage process is strongly influenced by the process of healing and that this process must be included in any model of the fatigue process.
the mechanism of healing of microcracks is the reorientation of the bitumen and aggregates in the microcrack zone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fatigue process in asphalt concrete is a process of damage growth and healing.
the surface energy of a mixture is a key factor for both fracture and healing.

fatigue damage is a result of competing processes of crack development and growth and crack healing and that the healing process is strongly influenced by the surface energy of the bituminous mixture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fatigue process is a complex process that is influenced by the competing processes of damage and healing.
the surface energy of the constituents of the mixture, as well as their compliance, must be considered when evaluating the fracture and healing of asphalt mixtures.
healing can play a very important role in fatigue and should be considered as an important design parameter for asphalt concrete.
